statement: Let n = len(arr). For each c with 0 <= c < k, let m_c be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and i mod k = c mod k, and let A_c be the sequence (arr[c], arr[c+k], ..., arr[c+k*(m_c-1)]). Let L_c be the maximum length t for which there exist integers 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{t-1} < m_c with A_c[j_0] <= ... <= A_c[j_{t-1}]. Then the function returns a result r and r = n - (L_0 + L_1 + ... + L_{k-1}).
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers; counts and sums in the specification are mathematical and do not overflow.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= n - k.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers.

statement: If arr is K-increasing, meaning that for every index i with k <= i < n we have arr[i-k] <= arr[i], then the function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = 0, arr is K-increasing: for every index i with k <= i < n, arr[i-k] <= arr[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an array b of length n of positive 64-bit integers such that: (a) b is K-increasing, so b[i-k] <= b[i] for every k <= i < n; (b) for every c with 0 <= c < k, if A_c and L_c are defined as in spec_1, then exactly L_c indices i with i mod k = c mod k satisfy b[i] = arr[i]; and (c) exactly r indices i with 0 <= i < n satisfy b[i] != arr[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every array b of length n of positive 64-bit integers that is K-increasing, meaning b[i-k] <= b[i] for every k <= i < n, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and b[i] != arr[i] is at least r.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers.

statement: If the call k_increasing(arr, k) returns r and the call k_increasing(arr', k) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. Let c0 be an integer with 0 <= c0 < k and let d be an integer. Define arr' by arr'[i] = arr[i] + d when i mod k = c0 mod k, and arr'[i] = arr[i] otherwise. Assume 1 <= arr'[i] <= n and arr'[i] is a 64-bit signed integer for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: For each c with 0 <= c < k, let A_c be the sequence of arr values in residue class c, as in spec_1. Let B be the number of c in 0 <= c < k for which A_c is not non-decreasing. Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= B.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. All values are 64-bit signed integers.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = n - k.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies n >= 1, n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, and 1 <= arr[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n. For every c with 0 <= c < k and every t with 0 <= t+1 < m_c, where m_c is the number of indices in residue class c, assume arr[c+k*t] > arr[c+k*(t+1)]. All values are 64-bit signed integers.
